sense: a small change made to fit or work better

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.120: mūtātiōnem facere, to make a change (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The general word for a change; Latin rather says what was changed, with the verb (pauca mūtāre), or an ablative absolute, as in the example.
For a change that puts a fault right, not for one that only adapts.
A scholars’ formula, not a classical one: “the things to be changed having been changed”.

phrases.english: With a few adjustments, I approve the plan.

sources: Lewis & Short: mutatio · Lewis & Short: emendatio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 254, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
